summary: Re-verified FBA deletion consistency fix (iteration 13 follow-up). Updated test_03 to match the NEW rule (reversal fires as soon as no remaining tx with fulfillment_type='FBA' exists for the order, even if a non-FBA expense still shares the order_id) and added test_04 as a sanity check for non-FBA order deletes. All 4 pytest cases PASS against the preview URL. The previously failing partial-order scenario is now green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L658 (bulk-delete) and L742 (single delete) now correctly collect refs for ANY deleted doc with an order_id — fulfillment_type filter removed. Fix is minimal and localized.

fba.py cleanup_deleted_fba_sales keeps a count_documents({..., fulfillment_type:'FBA'}) guard, so lingering non-FBA rows (expense fees) no longer keep the FIFO allocation alive. Reversal is still gated on `remaining==0 FBA txs`, which is the intended new semantics.
Minor: delete_transaction returns reversed_allocations even for pure non-FBA deletes (always 0) — consistent and documented via test_04.
No regressions observed in the 4 tested flows (single-delete, bulk-delete, partial-order, non-FBA order delete).
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_fba_delete_scenario.py (rewrote test_03 for new rule, added test_04 non-FBA sanity)
seed_data_creation: Each run creates isolated TEST_FBA_DEL_<rand> stores and TEST-SKU-* lots; stores are deleted on teardown. Real 'ng' store untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: FBA delete/cleanup regression lives in /app/backend/tests/test_fba_delete_scenario.py. Semantics as of iter14: reversal fires when zero remaining txs with fulfillment_type=='FBA' exist for (store_id, order_id), regardless of whether the deleted doc itself was FBA. lot_status values: OPEN/DEPLETED/CLOSED (uppercase). allocation status: active/reversed. Run with: `env REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... python -m pytest backend/tests/test_fba_delete_scenario.py -v -o addopts=`
rca of the issue: Iteration 13 failure root cause (now FIXED in server.py): refs for cleanup_deleted_fba_sales were filtered by fulfillment_type=='FBA'. Non-FBA expense rows (added via POST /api/transactions, which has no fulfillment_type field) sharing the same order_id never contributed to refs, so reversal was never attempted. Fix drops the filter; cleanup_deleted_fba_sales itself does the authoritative 'any FBA tx still on this order?' check. Verified: deleting the sole FBA sale on a partial order now correctly reverses the allocation and restores the lot (test_03). Deleting the leftover non-FBA expense afterwards is a no-op (reversed_allocations=0, 200 OK) — test_04 confirms.
